content.outcome: Render the governed Markdown corpus faithfully in the published documentation site, including tables and anchor IDs, while preserving source authority and deterministic publication.

classification.reason: The renderer affects every public documentation page and release package but does not change canonical MRD semantics.

authority_model: Generated Markdown remains the governed publication source consumed by the site renderer.
The HTML site and release archive remain deterministic downstream views with no semantic authority.
Only narrowly validated anchor markup is passed through; other source text remains HTML-escaped.
requirements: R1: Markdown tables MUST render as semantic HTML tables rather than literal pipe text.
R2: Governed span/div anchor identifiers MUST remain functional and MUST NOT be displayed as escaped markup.
R3: Fenced code, ordered and unordered lists, blockquotes, headings, paragraphs, links, inline code, strong emphasis, and emphasis MUST render consistently.
R4: Table, code, blockquote, list, and mobile presentation MUST remain readable without changing document semantics.
R5: Regenerated search, site, and release artifacts MUST remain deterministic and pass canonical verification.
implementation_plan: P1: Add failing renderer regression coverage for representative governed Markdown formatting.
P2: Replace the line-only renderer with bounded block and inline Markdown handling.
P3: Add readable responsive CSS for the supported formatting primitives.
P4: Rebuild search, site, and release artifacts and scan the full corpus for unrendered supported Markdown.
P5: Run canonical verification, review, publish, and observe Pages deployment.
verification_criteria: V1: Representative renderer tests cover anchors, tables, code, lists, blockquotes, inline formatting, and horizontal rules.
V2: Specification HTML contains no escaped governed span anchors, raw table separators, raw code fences, or raw bold markers.
V3: Current generated specification pages contain semantic tables and preserved anchor IDs.
V4: scripts/verify.ps1 passes after rebuilding all affected generated outputs.
V5: GitHub Pages deploy succeeds after merge.

tasks.text: Reproduce and characterize the site formatting defect.
Implement and verify full supported-format rendering and presentation.
Publish, merge, observe Pages deployment, and reconcile closeout.

risks: Over-broad raw HTML passthrough could weaken output safety; passthrough is restricted to validated anchor elements.
Renderer changes affect many deterministic generated files and therefore require site/search/release regeneration together.

verification: TDD regression test failed against the previous line-only renderer and passed after implementation.
Full generated Markdown corpus scan covered tables, anchor IDs, fenced code, ordered lists, blockquotes, inline formatting, and links.
Regenerated specification HTML contains 56 semantic tables and 328 preserved span anchor IDs, with zero escaped specification anchors, raw table separators, raw code fences, or raw bold markers.
Full scripts/verify.ps1 passed after rebuilding documentation search, site, and deterministic release artifacts.
reviews: Automated review routes returned EvidenceError on the large generated diff; manual fallback review found no unsafe raw-HTML passthrough beyond validated span/div anchor IDs and no unsupported Markdown construct used outside fenced code in the governed corpus.
